chunks: From al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi' from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abu al-Bakhtari from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said:
Fighting is of two types: Fighting for the people of polytheism, from whom they are not dismissed until they accept Islam or pay the jizyah with their own hands while they are subdued.
With their own hands while they are subdued.
And fighting for the people of deviation, from whom they are not dismissed until they return to the command of Allah or are killed.
ai.seo_question: What are the two types of fighting described in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted through Ali ibn Abi Talib, delineates the jurisprudential distinction between fighting polytheists (ahl al-shirk) and deviants (ahl al-zaygh), such as the Khawarij. While the former requires submission to Islamic sovereignty via Islam or jizyah, the latter must be compelled to return to the Imam's command (fi' ila amr Allah) or be killed, reflecting the Shia emphasis on internal political unity and correct doctrine. This classification underpins the strategic approach to civil wars and rebellions within the Shia legal tradition.
